newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says 46 dead in Kurdish rebel conflict.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says 46 dead in Kurdish rebel conflict.

text.p: Fourty-one Kurdish rebels and five members of the Turkish security forces have died in separate clashes in southeast Turkey in the last three days, Turkish security officials said on Monday.

The wife of a local leader of the coalition government's conservative wing died in hospital after being shot in the head at home in the southeast on Friday, hospital sources said. Her husband said she was hit by gunfire from a police post.
The regional governor's office in the city of Diyarbakir said in a statement that 41 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas and five members of the security forces had been killed in six provinces.
Some of the heaviest fighting was in the province of Sirnak, near the mountainous Iraqi border.
Huseyin Ozalp, chairman of a local branch of the True Path Party (DYP) said the shot that killed his 60-year-old wife was fired from a gendarmerie post in the town of Mazgirt.
"Shots were fired from the police station at our house," Ozalp told Reuters. "Bullets hit the house and one of them hit my wife," he said.
Security officials in the area said it was difficult to say who shot his wife because she was hit in crossfire during a clash with the PKK.

The statement from the governor's office did not report any fighting in or around Mazgirt. Ozalp, who says there were no guerrillas in the area at the time, has asked a prosecutor to investigate the killing.
The DYP of Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller is in coalition with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party.
More than 21,000 people have died in 12 years of conflict between security forces and the rebels, fighting for autonomy or independence.
